title: SYSK Selects: How Pizza Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun-style episode (introduced by Chuck as his pick for the week) about pizza. The hosts cover pizza history from ancient flatbreads in Greece and Naples, the tomato's arrival in Italy, Queen Margherita and the Margherita pizza legend, Italian immigration and early American pizzerias (Lombardi's, Shakey's, Pizza Hut), dough ingredients (flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar, shortening) and the New York water debate, sauce/cheese/topping build order and regional styles (New York, Chicago deep dish, Neapolitan with EU protection, California, Greek, Sicilian), oven types, international toppings, pizza industry statistics, the Ray's pizza name dispute, record-setting pizzas, and listener mail about a road-trip accident. Hosts also promote a Comic Con live show and trivia night in New York.

entities.name: Stuff You Should Know Comic Con live show

segments.title: Opening banter and pizza consumption
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the episode as his select pick. The hosts chat about how much pizza they eat, favorite local Atlanta pizza place Antico, and the basics that pizza is bread, cheese and sauce.

segments.title: Origins of pizza and the tomato
segments.summary: The hosts trace pizza back to flatbreads in Greece and to Naples, where the word pizza was first used. They discuss how peasants ate cheap bread-based dishes and how tomatoes arrived in Italy from the New World, including their early reputation as poisonous.

segments.title: Queen Margherita and pizza spreading to America
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Margherita pizza legend, in which a Naples pizza maker made a tomato, mozzarella and basil pizza for Queen Margherita in 1889. They then cover Italian immigrants bringing pizza to American cities and early pizzerias such as Lombardi's in New York.

segments.title: Pizza chains: Shakey's and Pizza Hut
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the rise of American pizza chains after World War Two, naming Shakey's as the first chain and Pizza Hut, founded in Kansas, with its name said to come from its hut-shaped building.

segments.title: Dough ingredients and gluten
segments.summary: The hosts explain the core dough ingredients of flour, water and yeast, with optional salt, sugar and shortening. They note that high-gluten flour gives pizza its structure and that gluten-free pizza is a poor substitute in their view.

segments.title: New York water and the oven debate
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the theory that New York pizza tastes better because of its tap water, sourced from the Catskills. They cite Mario Batali's view that the seasoned oven matters too, and a blind test in which people preferred New York-made crust.

segments.title: Yeast fermentation and making dough
segments.summary: The hosts explain how yeast eats sugars and releases gas to make dough rise. They describe kneading, proofing, and retarding dough in the refrigerator for up to three to five days.

segments.title: Sauce, cheese, toppings and regional styles
segments.summary: The hosts discuss build order for New York, white pizza and garlic butter sauce, and personal topping preferences. They then compare Chicago deep dish, which is built in reverse, with Sicilian and Greek styles.

segments.title: Neapolitan pizza standards and EU protection
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Neapolitan pizza standards, including its round shape, thin center, crust limits, wood-fired oven requirements and San Marzano tomatoes, along with EU protected status granted in December 2009. They also mention California-style pizza.

segments.title: International toppings and pizza statistics
segments.summary: The hosts list unusual toppings from Russia, Japan, India, Brazil and Costa Rica. They then cite US pizza statistics, including about three billion pizzas sold each year and chicken overtaking pepperoni as the top topping.

segments.title: Ray's Pizza name dispute and Domino's history
segments.summary: The hosts explain the history of the many New York pizzerias using the name Ray's, which began with Ralph Cuomo's Famous Original Ray's, and a trademark effort. They also discuss Domino's dropping its thirty-minutes-or-less guarantee and founder Tom Monaghan's views.

segments.title: Record pizzas
segments.summary: The hosts discuss expensive pizzas, including a gold-topped pizza and a $450 Vancouver pizza with lobster and caviar. They also cover the largest pizza ever made in Havana, Florida, and the longest pizza delivery from London to Melbourne in 2004.

segments.title: Live show and trivia announcements
segments.summary: Hosts promote a live podcast at Comic Con in New York on October 12 and a trivia night at the Cutting Room in the Flatiron District.

segments.title: Listener mail: road trip and accident
segments.summary: A listener named Annie describes a family road trip where she played the music, and her brother's horn honk caused a senior driver to brake, leading to a minor rear-end accident with no injuries.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts ask for listener stories and direct listeners to social media and the website.
